Then Sami Jumppanen presented her with a considerably more danceable instrumental, and “Fortress of Fools” became something else entirely. PLATRONiC build three new versions of ‘Fortress of Fools’ For the new EP, they have gone back to the song and, appropriately enough, given it three new “dresses.” The first, “The Dark Electro Country Dress,” is a collaboration with On Moral Ends, the Linköping-based electronic project of Swedish songwriter, singer and multi-instrumentalist Andreas Svensson. His work moves through different electronic and alternative styles, making the collaboration a rather unusual match for PLATRONiC’s futurepop side. For “The Synthpop Mashup Dress,” PLATRONiC worked with Finnish keyboardist, producer and remixer Imppu from Lahti. His work stretches from danceable synthpop to more cinematic electronic sounds, and he has also created remixes and reworks for former Kraftwerk member Wolfgang Flür. The third version stays with Kay and Sami themselves: “The Dark Medieval Gothic Dress.” According to PLATRONiC, “Fortress of Fools” spent several weeks in the Top 10 of both the Klangwald Charts and GEWC following its release earlier this year. The track reached #8 in the Klangwald Charts. The video for “Fortress of Fools” was filmed in Savonlinna, Finland, and Alicante, Spain, and was created and produced by PLATRONiC. PLATRONiC formed in 2020 and consists of German singer-songwriter and co-producer Kay Burden and Finnish composer and producer Sami Jumppanen. Side-Line readers may also know the duo from “How To Ride The Wave,” which appeared earlier this year on Side-Line’s The Freya Files Ukraine benefit compilation. “The Emperor’s New Clothes” tracklist: 1. “Fortress of Fools – The Dark Electro Country Dress” (PLATRONiC & On Moral Ends) 2. “Fortress of Fools – The Synthpop Mashup Dress” (PLATRONiC & Imppu) 3. “Fortress of Fools – The Dark Medieval Gothic Dress” (PLATRONiC) Before the three new “dresses” arrive, “Fortress of Fools” already has its own visual counterpart. “The Emperor’s New Clothes” is available to pre-save via DistroKid ahead of its 16 October release. About PLATRONiC PLATRONiC released the single “Now!” in June 2022, followed by the EP “The Healing” in April 2023 and a cover of Depeche Mode’s “The Things You Said” that August. A reworked version of their debut single “Pride” followed in June 2024, then the winter single “Winter Stores” that December. In March 2025, they released the teaser video for “How to Ride the Wave,” and in December 2025 contributed a cover of Depeche Mode’s “But Not Tonight” to the “In Your Memory 2” tribute compilation. “Fortress of Fools” followed in March 2026 as the duo’s most recent original single, ahead of “The Emperor’s New Clothes” EP arriving on 16 October.

items.body: Finnish electropunk duo I Think I Broke Something releases the single “Decadence” on 7 October 2026. The track is the third single from the duo’s upcoming EP “Another Escape,” due November 5, and the release will be marked with a show at Semifinal in Helsinki the same day. The band calls “Decadence” one of its most accessible tracks to date: “In our world, Decadence is a fairly straightforward electro-industrial punk track. You could describe it as a collision between Viagra Boys and The Prodigy, while still doing its own weird thing in its own universe. It’s probably one of the most radio-friendly tracks we’ve ever made.” Decadence by I Think I Broke Something “Decadence” follows “Illegal,” released August 6, and “Heads Up,” released September 9, as the third single from “Another Escape” ahead of the EP’s November 5 release. “Decadence” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and Spotify. About I Think I Broke Something I Think I Broke Something, also known as ITIBS, is a Helsinki-based duo made up of Jouni and Miika, active since 2014. The project debuted with the EP “Superman Sabotage Clan” and has since released three full-length albums, including “Still Not Going To,” announced for an October 26, 2022 release as the duo’s third LP, alongside numerous singles and remixes through various labels. That album cycle included the singles “Astral,” released September 2022, “Corpse,” released April 2023, and “Raw,” released July 2023. ITIBS describes its sound as a distorted electronic hybrid that draws on The Prodigy, 3TEETH and Nine Inch Nails and mixes explosive electronics with metal-heavy weight. The duo lists collaborations with The Prodigy’s Maxim, DJ Hyper and Zardonic. “Decadence,” released October 7, follows “Illegal” and “Heads Up” as the third single from the EP “Another Escape,” due November 5 alongside the band’s release show at Semifinal in Helsinki.

She released the nine-track spoken word dark ambient album “Make Yourself the Lie” on September 8, 2026, as a free, name-your-price download via VūMantra Records, the Berlin label founded in 2019 by Vince Gagliardi, who also records as The Nent and LAGÁN. Ms Xxan handles writing, performance, composition and production on her own across both releases. With “shaper of decrepitude.”, she returned to self-releasing directly on Bandcamp, pairing the title track with “ghosted.” as a quick follow-up to the VūMantra album.

items.body: We all want something better, bright and shiny dust. Fake names to hide within, blind among the rust Northeastern Pennsylvania has always seemed peculiarly suited to its own species of Gothic, where abandoned coal mines, crumbling factories, old churches, and stubborn little towns exist in uneasy communion with the American Dream. There is something metaphysically peculiar about a landscape whose prosperity was excavated from beneath its own feet, leaving the earth hollow and its inhabitants contemplating what remains. Here, the Gothic requires neither medieval castles nor European aristocrats. It grows naturally from industrial decay, Catholic guilt, Appalachian folklore, and the peculiar American talent for building civilizations atop buried disasters. Under such circumstances, making strange, sinister music seems less like an artistic decision than a perfectly reasonable response to one’s surroundings. Which brings us to ZEU, pronounced “zoo,” the musical alter ego of Matthew Zedolik of Wilkes-Barre, who has apparently decided that the region’s accumulated ghosts could use a backing band. There are few things more dangerous to public decency than a man left alone in a recording studio with a guitar, a head full of questionable ideas, and absolutely nobody around to tell him when to stop. Sometimes the result is genius. Zedolik writes, plays, records, and produces everything himself, an arrangement capable of yielding either magnificent obsession or twelve tracks of a man arguing with his presets. Fortunately, he seems to have made peace with his machinery, although his relationship with the rest of civilization remains questionable. Zedolik describes his approach as “’80s-era Springsteen meets Billy Idol, Depeche Mode, and Sisters of Mercy.” Which sounds like a barroom dare issued after somebody fed the jukebox three dollars and locked all the exits. Imagine the Boss borrowing Andrew Eldritch’s wardrobe, Billy Idol stealing the getaway car, and Martin Gore sitting in the back seat contemplating several regrettable romantic decisions. On Blind Among The Rust and Beyond Life and Death, ZEU takes that peculiar family reunion somewhere considerably less respectable. The songs inhabit the cracked asphalt between Tom Waits and The Gun Club, with the skeletal guitar menace of Rowland S. Howard and the diseased theatrical instincts of Foetus lurking nearby. There is something wonderfully disreputable about the combination, a species of surf goth that sounds as though somebody dragged a rockabilly band through a cemetery and subsequently denied them access to decent amplifiers. Zedolik’s growling vocals come crawling out of the arrangements with the nicotine-stained authority of a man who has seen the bottom of several bottles and found the conversation there surprisingly agreeable. Echoing guitars suggest desert highways, abandoned dance halls, and the occasional questionable roadside establishment, while atmospheric synthesizers introduce an industrial chill. Beneath the Gothic furnishings sits a garage-rock impulse, loose enough to suggest spontaneous combustion and sufficiently disciplined to keep the songs from collapsing into glorious nonsense. His musical education explains some of this strange chemistry. Teenage metal bands supplied the muscle; The Ordinals taught him bass discipline; American Buffalo Ghost gave him considerable guitar mileage. Recording studies in New York subsequently sharpened his understanding of arrangement and spatial dynamics. The accumulated experience gives these recordings their peculiar sense of purpose, even when the music appears headed toward some spectacularly unpleasant destination. Listen below: Blind Among The Rust / Beyond Life and Death by Zeu Following July’s full-length Existor, these two singles, released through Everything Evaporated, suggest an artist increasingly comfortable inhabiting his own peculiar corner of Pennsylvania Gothic. Somewhere between the last call at a roadside tavern and the first light over a neglected graveyard, ZEU has found a promising place to conduct his business. The neighbours may have complaints. items.body: There is a particular kind of youthful ambition that treats a synthesizer’s limitations as somebody else’s problem. If the arrangement feels crowded, another drum track might settle the argument; if the equipment begins to struggle, perhaps it needs to be programmed harder. Baltimore’s Pygmy Children remember their earliest recordings with the affectionate candor of two people who have since learned exactly what they were putting their machines through. More than thirty years later, those experiments are getting a fresh listen. Out now through Re:Mission Entertainment, Malignant: Redux revisits the electro-industrial duo’s 1994 debut album, Malignant, and the preceding 1993 EP, Facedown. Released October 2, the collection brings brothers Pete and Brian Roper back to the recordings that introduced them to the American industrial underground, with the digital edition collecting both releases in full. Originally recorded at Hit and Run Studios in Rockville, Maryland, with engineer Steve Carr, the material has received its first official remaster from Jeff Mortimer at JM Mastering. Brian Roper supplies the Redux artwork, completing a return to a period when the duo’s appetite for dense arrangements regularly outpaced the resources at their disposal. The brothers describe those sessions with refreshing frankness: “Admittedly, the record sounds pretty raw. We were novices trying to create something multi-layered and frenetic, working with what we had and probably not fully knowing what the hell we were doing, just going for it. Some of the synths were being pushed to the point of voice exhaustion, while multiple drum tracks pounded away simultaneously. Looking back, some editing was probably in order, but the intention was always there. We may not have hit the target exactly, but the aim was definitely there.” That willingness to admit the excess is part of the appeal. Their account describes two musicians learning through accumulation, pursuing an idea until the equipment itself began to object. The early titles suggest a similarly restless approach: Core moves between Resistance and Meltdown, while Facedown appears in Reflex, Manic, Bootstamp, and Dead versions across the digital collection. Even the track listing seems reluctant to leave an experiment alone. For Re:Mission founder Wes Turner, the release also carries a personal connection. Pygmy Children helped shape his taste in dark electronic music during the 1990s; three decades on, his label is releasing both their new work and these formative recordings. Turner now gets to put the records that helped educate him back into other listeners’ hands. Listen to Malignant : Redux below: Malignant : Redux by Pygmy Children Pygmy Children first surfaced with Facedown on Noname/Noslogan Productions, following it with Malignant before moving on to Deconstruct, released by Cleopatra in 1995, and Low Life Dream, issued through Sub/Mission Records and Out Of Line in 1998. After years away, the brothers returned in 2025 through Re:Mission with Coincidental Strategies, accompanied by singles including I Have No Name and Signal Unknown. Their recent single Proof in Lies, which we covered in August, leads their forthcoming fifth studio album, Into The Silence. With new material underway, Malignant : Redux offers a timely return to the duo’s beginnings. The brothers can now afford to smile at their early excesses, though the synthesizers they used back then may still be entitled to an apology. Malignant : Redux is available digitally and on CD via Re:Mission Entertainment. Order here or find additional listening options here. Limited digipak CD: An edition of 100 copies, containing Malignant plus Fear, the B-side from the Facedown EP, with the digital edition included. Three-CD autographed bundle: Malignant : Redux alongside autographed original pressings of Malignant and Facedown, plus the digital edition. Limited to 25 bundles, with US shipping only. items.body: In this extract, taken from the chapter “No EPI, No Nico, No Andy”, Richie Unterberger explores the troubled reception of The Velvet Underground & Nico on its release in 1967 As Eric Emerson’s frivolous lawsuit played out, The Velvet Underground & Nico continued to be plagued by Verve Records’s ineffective promotion. Its infamous “So far underground, you get the bends!” tagline exemplified how little understanding it had of how to market such an unusual yet groundbreaking record. “What happens when the daddy of Pop Art goes Pop Music?” the same ad asked. “The most underground album of all! It’s Andy Warhol’s hip new trip to the current subterranean scene. Sorry, no home movies. But the album does feature Andy’s Velvet Underground (they play funny instruments). Plus his this year’s Pop Girl, Nico (she sings, groovy). Plus an actual Warhol banana on the front cover (don’t smoke it… peel it)! The Velvet Underground, produced by Andy Warhol, is now available at record stores across the country. Just bring your own plain brown wrapper.” More aggravating was the continued general lack of radio airplay for the banana album, even on underground stations, in New York and elsewhere. In a 1981 interview with The New Musical Express, Sterling Morrison claimed local radio refused to even run advertisements for the album “because it was about drugs and sex and perversion”. In a radio interview promoting his 1976 LP Rock And Roll Heart, Lou Reed told Philadelphia’s WMMR that progressive FM stations wouldn’t run commercials for the record because of “Heroin”. To keep this in perspective, radio ads for such albums weren’t as common in 1967 as they’d be within a few years, and it’s not even certain Verve made many, or any. The 22 July issue of Record World reported that a radio spot advertising the LP would be available 15 August but if one was made, it still hasn’t circulated. “I remember being probably the only person that had ever played “Heroin” on the radio,” Richard Goldstein says. “Every now and then I’d get invited by Murray The K to the studio to play records. I would bring in the most unusual music I could find to play on his show. One night I played “Heroin”. And he was completely apoplectic, just completely apoplectic. Especially by the length of the song!” In the UK, Record Retailer moralised that “Heroin” was “distasteful, damaging to the industry’s image and should be banned” – though, perversely, it also singled out the LP’s least commercial track for praise, advising, “Try “European Son To Delmore Schwartz” – an excellent example of improvisation”. Even WBAI’s Bob Fass, later cited by Morrison as the only DJ in New York to give the banana album substantial exposure, was wary of airing “Heroin”. As a public radio station that was part of the progressive Pacifica network, WBAI had far less pressure to either be commercial or avoid controversy, but Fass still had reservations. At the time, he explains, he was under the impression the song was “part of something you might call ‘heroin chic’, which I thought was a very bad thing – making heroin like something attractive and mysterious in a dark corner that people should try to dig into. I was angry about it. I thought, ‘Why is this guy romanticising something that’s such a plague?’ In the right context, I would play it, but after there had been a putdown of heroin. As I listen to it now, it doesn’t make heroin sound romantic. It’s just a kind of a true depiction of what happens in the body of the addict as they wait for the connection. I think Lou Reed is one of the four or five authentic geniuses on the music scene, and I’m sorry that I didn’t listen to his stuff as carefully as I should have.” As Morrison noted, Fass did play other material from the record, and Bob confirms, “I played “All Tomorrow’s Parties” a lot, and “Femme Fatale”, “I’ll Be Your Mirror”.” As for Murray The K’s violent reaction to the sheer length of “Heroin”, Fass rejoins with amusement, “The length was something that I looked for. I wanted music to break that three minute sonnet form.” As for other outlets than Fass or Goldstein’s shows, feels Richard, “Given the material on this record, of course they wouldn’t play it. It wasn’t just because of the contents, but also the musical sophistication, [which] was way beyond anything that pop radio would have countenanced. I don’t know if [The Velvets] ever talked to me about that; I don’t think they did. I certainly would have told them, ‘Yeah, right. It’s gonna take a long time before this stuff is playable.’” But there were exceptions, even back in 1967. “The commercial ‘hip station’, which was WOR-FM, the first New York FM rock station, never played one Velvet note that I’m aware of,” remembers Scott Kempner, later to play guitar in The Dictators and The Del Lords. “However, WFMU, the Upsala College station outta [northern New] Jersey, which still is going loud and proud, played them, or... at least one show did. There was a show called Kokaine Karma, hosted by Dennis Frawley and Bob Rudnick; they loved The Velvets. Frawley and Rudnick played [their first LP] like it was a hit album.” According to Morrison, even Bob Fass stopped playing the album after the group turned down an invite to play a bail fund benefit at Tompkins Square Park in the East Village. The Velvet Underground had played a benefit for WBAI itself at the Cheetah Club in April on the same bill as Tiny Tim, but that didn’t grant them a reprieve. “That was how I made a lot of decisions,” acknowledges Fass. “If the band wasn’t political and they didn’t want to protest against the war, I thought they were ripping off the culture. I was very convinced that everything I did had to be either on the side of what I considered to be life or death.” Sterling was still angry about the incident when he was interviewed by Bill Bentley for an Austin Sun story in 1975. “We asked them, ‘By the way, who’s the benefit for?’ They said, ‘The people who get busted for grass and acid.’ We thought that was kind of curious. We asked them, ‘What about the people busted for junk and speed?’ They said, ‘Oh, no, those are bad drugs.’ How idiotic. Bad drugs – all of a sudden there are ‘bad drugs’. We told them either they bail everybody out, or we don’t play.” Although Morrison also told Bentley “we were very much known for playing benefits”, and The Velvet Underground had played benefits for the Cinematheque and WBAI, Reed didn’t seem eager to be involved with them a couple of years later. “We don’t play benefits,” he said in a March 1969 interview with Howard Smith of New York radio stations WABC and WPLJ. “I don’t believe in benefits, because I don’t believe in the people the benefits are for.” Whatever their true stance on the issue, this was apparently one instance in which the band’s relatively apolitical stance cost them appreciable media exposure. In his Austin Sun interview, Morrison asserted that after they turned down the WBAI benefit, “The result was that the ban was complete: a total blackout in New York City. Our altruism got in the way of our airplay. Any success in New York was through television [perhaps thinking of their brief clips on CBS and WNET] and newspapers. It had nothing to do with the legitimate outlet, which is radio. The music simply was not heard. The thing I’m most pissed about is that we were banned in New York for three years: 66 to 69, inclusive. Right up front, we were excluded from any FM radio play. AM was already out of the question: no music and no advertising. In our home city, the media capital of Earth, the native sons are banned.” As perverse payback, The Velvet Underground refused to play in New York at all for the next three years, with rare exceptions. Do What You Fear Most: The History Of The Velvet Underground is published by Omnibus Press. Read Byron Coley's review of the book in The Wire 512. Subscribers can also read the review online in the digital library.

items.body: EBM and synthpop duo Normal Bias released the single and video “Soft Power” on October 6, their first new material since 2024 debut album “Kingdom Come.” The track is the first glimpse of the band’s upcoming album “Ways of Keeping Clean,” due in 2027 via DKA Records. “Soft Power” is built on hard basslines, layered synths and vocals singer Matt Weiner delivers in a style the band’s press materials describe as “Hutchence-meets-Gahan.” The video, directed by Logan Devlin, combines live performance and stop-motion animation set against 16-bit, painterly desert landscapes with VHS-glitch treatment. Weiner sings in the video while bandmate Chris C performs amid a landscape of melting clocks and de-faced eyes. Normal Bias on the message behind ‘Soft Power’ The band described the song’s theme in a statement: “‘Soft Power’ confronts the numbing effects of propagandized multimedia addiction that looms over the modern world and enables the worst instincts of our leaders and institutions and leads us further into nowhere and nothing.” Normal Bias describe their own sound as “equal parts techno synthpop and ruthless venture capital,” wryly calling the project “a pump and dump scheme, mining the most bloodthirsty pieces of decades of electronic music and stripping it for parts.” “Soft Power” is available to stream and watch now. “Ways of Keeping Clean” is expected via DKA Records in 2027. About Normal Bias Normal Bias is the duo of Matt Weiner and Chris C, based partly in New York and partly in Atlanta. The band released its debut album “Kingdom Come” in 2024 through DKA and Synthicide, drawing on EBM and synthpop. They have shared stages with Nitzer Ebb, Boy Harsher, Pixel Grip, Buzz Kull, Nuovo Testamento, High Functioning Flesh and Phase Fatale, and are currently touring alongside Spike Hellis. “Soft Power” marks Normal Bias’ return after “Kingdom Come” and sets up “Ways of Keeping Clean,” the duo’s next full-length, slated for release via DKA Records in 2027.

items.body: New York-based musician Edley ODowd, formerly of Psychic TV, will release his second solo album, “Kowai-Yet,” on November 26, 2026 via the French label Arsenic Solaris. The ambient and experimental record follows his 2022 debut, “F(our)-Ward,” and arrives on vinyl and digital, with the Pink LP edition limited to 200 copies. ODowd recorded “Kowai-Yet” over three years in multiple locations. The album brings together material he made with collaborators he has worked with since leaving New York City to live closer to nature five years ago. The seven-track record shifts from the sound-collage approach of “F(our)-Ward” toward a more emotional register. “Where F(our)-Ward was more about sound collage, Kowai-Yet is about emotion,” ODowd says. “It’s infused with joy as well as a heaping dose of sadness.” The album’s title traces back to a single word. Describing a drive home on a summer night, ODowd recalls the sound of crickets against his car tires on humid pavement as both “sinister but compelling.” The Japanese word “kowai,” meaning “scary,” came to him first. At a stop sign, as the air went still, “quiet” followed, and the two merged into “Kowai-yet.” Individual tracks trace separate origins. “Heat” took shape through an improvised studio session in Los Angeles with engineer Joo Joo Ashworth, built from a drum pattern and expanded with analog electronics set against ODowd’s backwards saxophone. “Again” began as a more traditional song ODowd wrote alone. British musician Gore Tech later added a sharper beat, two guitarists contributed parts, and singer Zoah, whom ODowd met at a coffee shop along the Delaware River, added vocals and lyrics. “Arbiter” reworks stems ODowd had originally recorded for an unfinished song about his friend Lady Jaye Breyer P-Orridge. Its choruses use samples recorded during a 2000 trip to Nepal with Lady Jaye and Genesis P-Orridge, manipulated into the track. His Problem Addict collaborator Andrew Mann closes the song with guitar feedback. “Kowai-Yet” tracklist: 1. “Jamesey” 2. “Arbiter” 3. “Again” 4. “(Bruce Was) Kicked Out Of The Band” 5. “Heat” 6. “Sunrise” 7. “You’ll Never Know” Kowai-Yet release details “Kowai-Yet” is out November 26, 2026 via Arsenic Solaris as a digital album and a Pink LP limited to 200 copies. Both are available to pre-order on Bandcamp, where the track “Heat” is streaming now. Photo credits: Trevor Gregory. Kowai-Yet by Edley ODowd About Edley ODowd Edley ODowd grew up in the suburbs outside New York City and moved to Manhattan in the late 1980s, shortly after finishing high school. He got his start on a secondhand drum kit his mother bought him at a garage sale when he was 13. During a semester abroad in London in 1991, he joined the shoegaze band The Butterflies. Back in New York, he played drums and DJed for Toilet Boys, a band that wound down after a major European tour supporting the Red Hot Chili Peppers. In 2003, ODowd was instrumental in reviving Psychic TV, persuading Genesis P-Orridge to perform again. The reunited band’s first show took place at The Coral Room in New York City on December 5, 2003. ODowd founded the label Angry Love Productions after a self-funded Psychic TV EP sold out its 230 copies within two weeks. The “PTV3” lineup of Psychic TV played its final show on November 15, 2018. Alongside music, ODowd has worked as a graphic designer for major labels since 1993, taught courses at several universities in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and worked as a mental health counselor, including as a front-line worker during the COVID-19 pandemic. ODowd released his debut solo album, “F(our)-Ward,” as a self-released, ultra-limited cassette via Flesh Prison/DeathBed Tapes in 2022. Side-Line covered its expanded reissue, “F(our) ward,” released as a trifold-sleeved CD with three bonus tracks via the Italian label 13 on February 23, 2023. That same year, ODowd formed the death rock band Scorpion Tea with Christian Cruz, singer Anthony Diaz and bassist Fern Puma, signing to the label GIVE/TAKE. Side-Line covered the band’s debut single, “Scarlet Misquote,” in June 2023, ahead of the band’s self-titled debut album. ODowd now lives about an hour’s drive from New York City, where he continues to split his time between graphic design clients, band rehearsals and recording. “Kowai-Yet,” his second solo album, is set for release on November 26, 2026 via Arsenic Solaris.

items.body: Israeli gothic metal band Fatum Aeternum has rebuilt “P.W.Y.P.” for a streaming release, bringing the track back from their 2012 EP “The Sermon.” The self-released single went out digitally on 25 September 2026. The new version keeps the original ’80s glam-rooted guitar riff while adding aggressive male vocals, a female counter voice, cello and a full gospel choir. Where the 2012 recording leaned on social commentary, the rebuilt arrangement expands it into a more layered, theatrical gothic sound the band describes as a dark sermon. “P.W.Y.P.” is the second single in Fatum Aeternum’s renewed run of releases, following the comeback single “As Above, So Below” on 25 August 2026. That single introduced a new six-piece lineup – Steve Gershin, Evelyn Shor Gershin, Dr. Joe, Victor Grassiano, Max Datskovsky and Mark Muzykant – which also plays on “P.W.Y.P.” The track was recorded at Lodge Studios in Northampton, UK. Denis Saenko handled mixing and mastering, with additional mixing by Gershin; Tayo Olawepo arranged and recorded the choir. The band’s promotional materials cite Lacrimosa, Therion and Haggard as reference points. “P.W.Y.P.” is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music, Deezer and SoundCloud. About Fatum Aeternum Fatum Aeternum formed in Tel Aviv, Israel, in 2006, built around Steve Gershin on mandolin, bass and vocals, alongside Ze’ev Gut on fiddle and vocals and Olga Braverman on flute and vocals. The group’s first full lineup added Ilya Surnin on drums, Dan Yoffe on guitar and Rivka Aizenberg on viola, playing a self-described “renaissance metal” blend of folk and metal. Braverman left in 2007 and Gut in 2008, staying on as a guest musician as the band shifted toward a heavier, more electrified sound. Gershin considered disbanding the group in 2009 and recorded a memorial album of earlier material instead; Evelyn Shor Gershin joined permanently around the same time, stabilising the lineup. The band re-recorded its debut album “This Dream Is Dead” several times before releasing it on CD in 2011. On 24 September 2011, Fatum Aeternum played the 12th Children of the Night Gothic Festival in Kyiv, Ukraine, its first show outside Israel, sharing the bill with Waves Under Water and Diary of Dreams. The video for “Apocalypse Now” followed on YouTube in April 2012 and aired on MTV Israel’s “Headbangers Ball” that June. The band self-released the EP “The Sermon” in September 2012, recorded at Lodge Studios in Northampton, UK, and opened for Apoptygma Berzerk the same month before going on hiatus in 2013. Gershin and Evelyn Shor Gershin rebuilt the lineup with George Falk and Igor May in 2014, releasing the single “One Bastard” that April and the maxi-single “The Pain” later the same year. The EP “The Darkest Hour” followed in 2015, then “Mass Suicide of Human Race” in 2017 and “Singing Songs of Desperation” in 2020. Fatum Aeternum returned in 2026 after a three-year gap, a pause the band’s own site attributes to health issues within the group. The comeback single “As Above, So Below” arrived on 25 August 2026 with a new six-piece lineup of Gershin, Evelyn Shor Gershin, Dr. Joe, Victor Grassiano, Max Datskovsky and Mark Muzykant. “P.W.Y.P.,” a rebuilt version of the 2012 “The Sermon” track, follows as the second single in that renewed run.

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Heldautomat‘s new single “Liebe ist endlich” on October 9, 2026. It is the third single from the Dortmund, Germany duo’s debut album “Zwischen den Lichtern”, due October 23 on the same label. “Liebe ist endlich” (“Love is finite”) opens with a slow synthesizer introduction before settling into a synth-pop arrangement, with Christian Purwien’s vocals staying restrained throughout. The refrain states its theme directly: “Liebe ist endlich / Sie ist leider vergänglich” (“Love is finite / Unfortunately, it is transient”). Heldautomat describe the track on Bandcamp as a song with “no metaphors, no way out, no redemption. Just the quiet realisation that things come to an end.” Purwien writes the lyrics and sings. Kowa plays the synthesizers. Olaf Wollschläger produced the single. Club mix and video for ‘Liebe ist endlich’ The digital release also includes a “Videomix” of the duo’s first single, “Am ersten Tag”, and a club mix of “Liebe ist endlich” produced by Purwien & Kowa, Purwien and Kowa’s other recording project. Heldautomat also posted an official video for “Liebe ist endlich” on YouTube. “Liebe ist endlich” is open for digital pre-order on Bandcamp. Liebe ist endlich by Heldautomat About Heldautomat Heldautomat is the Dortmund, Germany duo of Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa, working with analogue synthesizers, piano and a drum machine alongside Purwien’s vocals. Purwien co-founded Second Decay in Witten in 1987 with Andreas Michael Sippel, after the pair had performed as Blue Velvet from 1985. Second Decay recorded entirely on analogue synthesizers and released albums including “Taste” (1994) and “The Hunt” (1998) before going quiet after 2002. Emmo.Biz Records has since reissued “The Hunt” on green double vinyl and “Taste” on a second double-LP edition. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Purwien & Kowa, a project with five albums behind it and a sixth, “Sechs”, in the works. The duo played the 18th Elektrisch Festival on February 27, 2026, in a set drawn 70 percent from Second Decay material. Heldautomat released its debut single, “Am ersten Tag“, on May 15, 2026. “Anders Sein” followed on August 14, reworking a song Sippel and Purwien wrote for Second Decay’s “Taste” in 1994. “Liebe ist endlich” is the third single, and precedes the October 23 album “Zwischen den Lichtern”, produced throughout by Olaf Wollschläger and including a cover of Nine Inch Nails‘ “Hurt”. A vinyl edition of the album, limited to 100 hand-signed copies, is available alongside the digital release.

items.body: Silence has a talent for passing itself off as peace. Two people can share a room, exchange the necessary pleasantries, and conduct an entire argument without troubling the air between them. Inside, every withheld accusation is already gathering speed. Given enough time, even “How was your day?” can begin to sound like a contact sport. Milan quartet October take that condition onto the ice in their video for Universe. The fourth single from their debut album, Dancing Like an Idiot, out now through Waddafuzz! Records, follows the uncomfortable distance between what a relationship looks like from the outside and what its participants are putting themselves through within it. A frozen surface can conceal considerable commotion, and October have enlisted a hockey team to give those private collisions a public airing. The song itself has a supple, sophisticated swing. A rhythmic bassline brings the new wave funk of Roxy Music and Japan to mind, its firm articulation keeping the groove grounded as sustained guitar tones stretch above it. The snare lands at deliberate intervals, leaving generous space around each strike. There is a progressive streak in the arrangement, a willingness to let the instrumental passages stretch and change shape without losing the underlying rhythm. Gianluca Villa sings in a silky upper register reminiscent of Peter Gabriel, his measured delivery building to increasingly impassioned peaks on the line “A Message from the stars.” A gentle guitar jangle carries the song forward, lifting some of its emotional weight. A string interlude zigzags through the arrangement as the vocal rises into a high croon, and tension builds until the full force of the performance comes crashing back. Directed and edited by Fabrizio Grasso, with concept and production by Davide Debenedetti for Filmico, the video makes that division visible. October perform on the rink beneath bright backlights, framed against rows of empty seats, while members of Sgularat Hockey Club Milano skate around them in yellow and black. The musicians hold their positions as the players accelerate, compete, and cut across the space between them. Pads, helmets, and sticks give anger and frustration a physical vocabulary; the ice supplies the emotional temperature. There is something both funny and painfully apt about bringing protective equipment into a love song. Here, the action surrounding the band becomes the argument nobody is having aloud: misunderstandings, thwarted attempts at connection, and the helplessness of trying to reach someone who has become difficult to recognise. Grasso lets the rink carry the metaphor, its broad white expanse accommodating all that activity without offering much warmth. Watch the video for Universe below: October formed in Milan in 2024, bringing together musicians whose backgrounds include Grandi Animali Marini, Il Fieno, NOA, and Egokid, alongside collaborations with Veracrash and I Ministri. Villa handles guitar and vocals, joined by bassist Dario Giordano, drummer Paolo Soffientini, and synth player Davide “dEbE” Debenedetti. Their debut was recorded at Casamedusa with Francesco Campanozzi and Frigo Studio with Francesco Ferrari, then mixed and mastered by Paolo Mauri. Released on March 30, 2026, Dancing Like an Idiot is available digitally and on vinyl. Listen to Universe below and order the album here. items.body: German darkwave artist Die Tödin releases a self-titled compilation on 30 October through Heartworm Press, the label founded by Cold Cave’s Wesley Eisold. The collection gathers nine recordings made between 2022 and 2025 and expands on Die Tödin’s earlier “Selected Singles” release on Minimalkombinat. Die Tödin said the compilation follows a difficult stretch of her life: “The last two years have been very difficult for me, so I want to draw a symbolic line under that period with this release.” She described the collection as a near-complete retrospective, calling it “almost everything Die Tödin has released to date.” Die Tödin’s self-titled compilation on Heartworm Press The release comes on white vinyl and on a Black Static vinyl edition limited to 200 copies. Both pressings include an 11-by-17-inch newsprint poster. The tracklist: Ich bin schon tot Angepasste Spießerschweine Wild Gift living that DSBM life Dissonanz des Lebens Im Schatten Verderben La Bruja / Die Geister, die ich rief Verderben by Die Tödin About Die Tödin Die Tödin records as a darkwave artist based in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Her back catalogue includes the “Selected Singles” release on Minimalkombinat, drawn together with other tracks from 2022 to 2025 into the self-titled compilation due 30 October on Cold Cave member Wesley Eisold’s Heartworm Press. The compilation, pressed on white and limited Black Static vinyl, becomes Die Tödin’s most complete release to date.

前出のラジオ局、フランス・ミュージックよりもう一本。ジャズ・ボーカリストのリズ・ライト（Lizz Wright）と、ピアニストのケニー・バンクスSr.（Kenny Banks Sr.）が初めて完全にデュオに徹して作ったアルバム『Nearness』について採り上げている。 ふたりの出会いは大学時代のアトランタ。以来20年以上、共同作業を重ねてきたという。収録されているのは、スピリチュアル、ジャズ・スタンダード、オリジナル曲。バンクスはピアノとオルガンを担当し、プロデューサーはChris Bruce、最終曲はア・カペラである。出典によれば、二人が教会で共に歩んだことと、ジャズ、R&B、即興への関心が、この作品の土台になっている。   教会という共通の場と、ジャズ・R&B・即興への関心。二つの水脈が長い協働のなかで重なってきたことが、スピリチュアルとスタンダードを一枚に並べる構成に表れているように思える。ピアノとオルガン、そして最後は声だけ。編成を絞った作りが、題名の「近さ」にそのまま重なる。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/lizz-wright-intime-proximite-1727454 旅の混乱が題になった─ クリス・デイヴィス・トリオ『Lost in Geneva』 ピアニストのクリス・デイヴィス（Kris Davis）が、ロバート・ハースト、ジョナサン・ブレイクとのトリオで、新作『Lost in Geneva』をリリースした。アルバムのタイトルは、旅のアクシデントの逸話に由来するという。 表題曲は、時差ぼけと不慣れな環境による混乱を喚起する曲である。2024年の『Run the Gauntlet』以来、3人は数えきれない時間を路上とステージで共にしてきた。 ピアノ・トリオは、三者の対話で成り立つ形式である。時間と場所を共有した経験の厚みが、題名や表題曲という形で作品に刻まれている。『Run the Gauntlet』から続く道中の記録として、並べて聴けるだろう。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/kris-davis-trio-complicite-amplifiee-par-la-desorientation-6244148 クリス・デイヴ、モノネオン、ジャスタス・ウェスト─11月、ビルボードライブ横浜・東京・大阪で ドラマーのクリス・デイヴ（Chris Dave）、ベーシストのモノネオン（MonoNeon）、ギタリストのジャスタス・ウェスト（Justus West）が、11月にビルボードライブの横浜・東京・大阪で公演を行う。 日程は11月17日が横浜、19日が東京、20日が大阪で、各日2ステージ（開演17:30・20:30）。告知文はこの公演を「ジャンルの境界を軽やかに越えた予測不能のセッション」と紹介。ドラム、ベース、ギターという三つの楽器の奏者が、三つの街で同じ顔ぶれの音を交わす。 出典：https://www.billboard-live.com/tokyo/show?event_id=ev-21707 ミシェル・ンデゲオチェロ『Synonym』─他人の歌を読み替える 英ガーディアン紙が、ミシェル・ンデゲオチェロ（Meshell Ndegeocello）の新作『Synonym』のレビューを掲載した。見出しは、ボブ・ディランからJ-Loまでの鮮やかなオールスターによる再解釈（原題：vivid all-star reinventions）。 レビューが具体的に挙げているのは、たとえば次のような例である。Cat Powerとの「Don’t You Want Me」はレゲエに作り替えられ、Callahanとの「With God on Our Side」が収められている。Anohniとの「I Got You Babe」は、音数を絞ったジャズ・アレンジ（原文：sparse jazz）になっている。さらにグラスパー（Glasper）の参加にも触れられている。 ジャズは、他ジャンルの曲を取り込み、自分たちの言葉で語り直すことを繰り返してきた。本作もまた、その伝統の延長に置いて聴くことができるだろう。 出典：https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/oct/01/meshell-ndegeocello-synonym-review-vivid-all-star-reinventions-of-everyone-from-bob-dylan-to-j-lo オスカー・ブラウン・ジュニア生誕100年、その遺産を語る 英国のジャズ情報サイトUK Jazz ジャズ・ボーカリストで作曲家のオスカー・ブラウン・ジュニアの生誕100年を記念する企画で、ブラウンの芸術的な遺産と影響が語られている。歌い手であり作曲家でもあった人物の仕事を、同じ歌い手が語る。節目の年にその名前に触れることは、残された作品を聴き直す入口にもなる。 items.body: David J, a co-founder, bassist and co-songwriter of the post-punk bands Bauhaus and Love and Rockets, releases the single “Requiem for the Rose Garden” on 51 Recordings on 8 October 2026. The song is a protest aimed at the Trump administration, built around the White House Rose Garden as a target that is both symbolic and literal. It is the first track confirmed from J’s new album “Postcards from the Afterlife,” due 27 November on double LP, CD and digital formats. David J on ‘Requiem for the Rose Garden’ J points to physical changes made at the White House since Donald Trump’s first term in office when he explains the song. “It’s basically a protest about Trump’s administration and the atrocities it has visited upon the USA,” he said. “In the context of the song, the Rose Garden at the White House can be seen as a symbolic metaphor, although it is also quite literal. I actually wrote it during Trump’s first term in office when he had that beautiful garden hacked up. Now, even more horror has been inflicted on it of course, and the elegant East Wing of the building completely decimated which is also highly symbolic.” The backing band on the track is Duende, a Detroit-based group J has worked with extensively in the past. “Requiem for the Rose Garden” streams on Spotify, Apple Music, Tidal, Deezer and Pandora via davidjhaskins.com. ‘Postcards from the Afterlife’ due in November on 51 Recordings “Postcards from the Afterlife” is a 14-song album featuring a revolving cast of musicians and numerous autobiographical references. J sums up its themes as circling the same idea from several angles: “essentially about the poignant persistence of connection, be it in life or in death. Schisms and transitions. Love found and love lost. Requiems, reflection and revelation.” Several tracks carry string arrangements, including a finale recorded with members of the Prague Symphony and Philharmonic Orchestras. The rest of the album moves between soulful material, hazy 1960s orchestral pop, European-style chanson and the alternative rock territory J is best known for. “Postcards from the Afterlife” is released on double LP, CD and digital on 27 November. Tour dates for David J David J tours the UK through December 2026, with additional shows in Portugal, Germany and Greece around the “Postcards from the Afterlife” release. 27 November – Porto, Portugal 28 November – Lisbon, Portugal 1 December – London, UK – Moth Club 2 December – Reading, UK – Face Bar 4 December – Hebden Bridge, UK – Trades Club 5 December – Liverpool, UK – Rough Trade 8 December – Edinburgh, UK – The Voodoo Rooms 9 December – Glasgow, UK – Stereo 10 December – Newcastle, UK – The Cluny 11 December – Birmingham, UK – Hare & Hounds 13 December – Brighton, UK – Daltons 15 December – Athens, Greece – Death Disco 17 December – Berlin, Germany – Frannz Club About David J David J, born David John Haskins on 24 April 1957 in Northampton, England, co-founded Bauhaus in 1978, playing bass and co-writing songs including the group’s debut single, “Bela Lugosi’s Dead.” He sang lead vocals on “Who Killed Mr Moonlight?” Bauhaus split in 1983 and has reformed periodically since. Before Love and Rockets, J spent two years as bassist and co-producer for The Jazz Butcher, led by Pat Fish, working on the albums “A Scandal in Bohemia” (1984) and “Sex and Travel” (1985). He formed Love and Rockets in 1985 with fellow former Bauhaus members Daniel Ash and his younger brother Kevin Haskins, playing bass and sharing vocals and songwriting across seven albums released between 1985 and 1998. Both bands have reformed at intervals since their original breakups. J maintained a solo career alongside both bands. He released “Etiquette of Violence” in 1983, “Crocodile Tears and the Velvet Cosh” in 1985 and the singles compilation “On Glass” in 1986. His 1990 album “Songs from Another Season” produced the single “I’ll Be Your Chauffeur,” which reached number one on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. “Urban Urbane” followed in 1992, then “Estranged” in 2003, “Not Long for This World” in 2011 and “An Eclipse of Ships” in 2014. His memoir, “Who Killed Mister Moonlight? (Bauhaus, Black Magick and Benediction),” was published by Jawbone Press in 2014. In 2019 J released the double LP “Missive to an Angel From the Halls of Infamy and Allure.” Side-Line covered the album’s single “I Only Hear Silence Now,” featuring Emily Jane White, alongside a run of 2020 tour dates that included Bauhaus shows at Primavera Sound and Release Athens Festival. “What The Patrons Heard,” a ten-track set of originals and covers recorded over 34 years and first issued to Patreon subscribers, followed on CD and digital on 25 March 2022, with a limited numbered vinyl edition. J’s triple album of archival demos, “Tracks from the Attic,” was announced in February 2024 and released that year. He self-released the spoken-word album “The Mother Tree,” recorded with the band RAQIA, on 6 June 2025. He returned to the “Tracks from the Attic” material in March 2026 with a companion album, “Tracks From the Attic Revisited,” which Side-Line discussed with him the following month in the interview “David J Opens the Attic.” This month’s single and the album that follows continue that run of archival and new recordings.

items.body: English musician Bruce Gilbert, a founding member of Wire, plays a solo live set at Café OTO in London on Friday 9 October 2026. The night is billed as “The Hotel presents…” and also features Rocheman and performance artist Finn Kennedy. Doors are at 7:30pm, with tickets priced from £13 for Café OTO members up to £20 on the door, available through the venue. The show is The Hotel’s third evening at Café OTO in 2026. Gilbert’s set previews a new album due from The Hotel later this year. Test pressings of the as-yet-unannounced record will be sold at the merch table. Finn Kennedy premieres a newly commissioned piece titled “Streams.” Rocheman closes the night with a full band set, performing as a quartet with Fred Lomas on lead guitar, Tom Powell on drums and Tom Wright on keyboards. Rocheman’s second album, “Basin,” was released on vinyl by The Hotel earlier in 2026, following the EPs “Angel Storm” and “Virtua Saint” on Mindseyerecords.xyz. The self-directed feature film “Taurus,” due in 2027, is among the artist’s forthcoming work. Tickets for The Hotel at Café OTO Tickets cost £13 for Café OTO members, £17 in advance and £20 on the door, available through the venue’s event page. About Bruce Gilbert Bruce Gilbert, born Bruce Clifford Gilbert on 18 May 1946 in Watford, England, co-founded Wire in London in 1976 alongside Colin Newman, Graham Lewis and Robert Gotobed, playing guitar in the band until he left in 2004, following the release of the album “Send.” After Wire’s first breakup in 1980, Gilbert formed a series of projects with bassist Graham Lewis, including Cupol, Dome, P’o and Duet Emmo. Side-Line covered the 2022 remastered reissue of Duet Emmo’s sole album, “Or So It Seems,” Gilbert’s trio recording with Lewis and Daniel Miller. Gilbert also worked with A.C. Marias, producing the single “Drop/So” in 1980 for the group’s Dome label and co-producing the 1989 album “One of Our Girls (Has Gone Missing),” sharing songwriting credit with Angela Conway. Gilbert’s solo albums include “This Way” (1984), “The Shivering Man” (1987) and “Ab Ovo” (1996), all released on Mute, followed by “Ordier” (2004), “Oblivio Agitatum” (2009, Editions Mego) and “Diluvial” (2013, Touch), a collaboration with BAW. He also performs as a DJ under the name DJ Beekeeper. Wire continued without Gilbert after his departure, releasing the mini-album “Nocturnal Koreans” in 2016. Gilbert now appears at Café OTO as part of The Hotel’s third London show of 2026, ahead of a new album the label is set to release later this year.

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Purwien & Kowa‘s new single “Italo-disco in San Francisco” on 9 October 2026, ahead of the German synth-pop duo’s sixth studio album, “Sechs,” due 23 October on the same label. The digital single carries four tracks: German and English versions of “Italo-disco in San Francisco,” an extended “Irgendwas ist immer (12″ Mix)” and a combined “German English Mashup 12″ mix” of the title track. Both language versions of the lyrics string together a run of 1980s references, naming figures including Lady Diana, Mikhail Gorbachev, Blondie, Phil Collins, Falco and Michael Jackson alongside songs such as “Blue Monday,” “Tainted Love,” “Like a Virgin,” “Take On Me,” “99 Luftballons,” “Forever Young” and “The Final Countdown.” “Italo-disco in San Francisco” mixes Italo disco, synthpop, New Wave and EBM, and follows the singles “Concorde” and “Hinter Glas” as the third preview of “Sechs.” Italo-disco in San Francisco by Purwien & Kowa About Purwien & Kowa Purwien & Kowa is a German synth-pop duo based in Dortmund formed by Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa. Purwien co-founded the electronic/darkwave act Second Decay in 1987, initially under the name Blue Velvet, together with Andreas Michael Sippel. Second Decay released the tape “Monochromes” in 1988 and the 12-inch “Killing Desire” in 1989, followed by “La Décadence Électronique” on CD in 1992, the “Hinter Glas” maxi-CD in 1993 and the album “Taste” in 1994. The band continued with “Der Nerv” in 1995, “Familiar” in 1997, “The Hunt” and “De Luxe” in 1998, “Hotels” in 1999 and “Kaltes, weißes Licht” in 2001, before pausing new material after the 2002 live release “Zwischenfall 1999.” Thomas Kowa, born Thomas Kowalzik in 1969 in Ludwigshafen am Rhein, joined the German synth-pop band No Comment in 1989 and has lived in Switzerland since 2007. He founded the label Nanopop in 2001, closing it in 2007 to focus on writing. Since 2012 he has published a series of crime novels and thrillers. His other current music projects include Nine Seconds and Emily Kinski’s dead. Purwien and Kowa began recording together as Purwien & Kowa, releasing the three-EP digital set “Drei” via Zwei Records in October 2018. The duo also co-hosts the Disko 80 podcast, which covers 1980s music and has featured more than 100 episodes with guests including Joachim Witt, Bernhard Lloyd of Alphaville and Marcus Meyn of Camouflage. Kowa separately co-hosts the “Krimi Schweiz” podcast on Swiss crime fiction. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Heldautomat, whose own single “Liebe ist endlich” reached Town & Towers Records on the same day as “Italo-disco in San Francisco.” The duo performed at the 18th Elektrisch Festival in 2026. Purwien & Kowa returned this year with the singles “Concorde,” “Hinter Glas” and “Italo-disco in San Francisco,” ahead of their sixth studio album, “Sechs,” produced by Olaf Wollschläger and due 23 October 2026 via Town & Towers Records.

items.body: Marilyn Manson’s second studio album, “Antichrist Superstar,” turns 30 this year. The band released the record on 8 October 1996 through Nothing and Interscope Records. A rock opera and concept album, it followed 1994’s “Portrait of an American Family” and the 1995 EP “Smells Like Children,” and was recorded over roughly eight months at Nothing Studios in New Orleans. The album was produced by Marilyn Manson together with Trent Reznor, Dave Ogilvie and Sean Beavan, with Ogilvie departing partway through the sessions and Beavan brought in to finish the record with the band. Guitarist Daisy Berkowitz left the group during recording and was replaced by Zim Zum shortly after the album’s completion, with bassist Twiggy Ramirez performing the majority of the guitar parts. The 16-track CD, split into three sections titled “The Heirophant,” “Inauguration of the Worm” and “Disintegrator Rising,” runs “Irresponsible Hate Anthem,” “The Beautiful People,” “Dried Up, Tied and Dead to the World,” “Tourniquet,” “Little Horn,” “Cryptorchid,” “Deformography,” “Wormboy,” “Mister Superstar,” “Angel with the Scabbed Wings,” “Kinderfeld,” “Antichrist Superstar,” “1996,” “Minute of Decay,” “The Reflecting God” and “Man That You Fear,” followed by a hidden track, “Empty Sounds of Hate.” Album artwork was designed by P. R. Brown using photography by Dean Karr. “Antichrist Superstar” debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 and has sold close to two million copies in the United States. Lead single “The Beautiful People” preceded the album on 22 September 1996 and reached number 26 on Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart and the top 20 of the UK Singles Chart, followed by second single “Tourniquet” on 8 September 1997, which peaked at number 28 in the UK. The album is the first installment of a trilogy the band completed with “Mechanical Animals” (1998) and “Holy Wood (In the Shadow of the Valley of Death)” (2000), and was supported by the year-long Dead to the World Tour. About Marilyn Manson Marilyn Manson formed in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, in 1989, when singer Brian Warner – who took the stage name Marilyn Manson – paired with guitarist Scott Putesky, known as Daisy Berkowitz. Performing initially as Marilyn Manson & the Spooky Kids, the group built a South Florida following through theatrical live shows, with a lineup that came to include bassist Brad Stewart (Gidget Gein), keyboardist Stephen Bier (Madonna Wayne Gacy) and drummer Fred Streithorst (Sara Lee Lucas). In 1993, Nine Inch Nails founder Trent Reznor signed the band as the first act on his Nothing Records label and produced their debut album, “Portrait of an American Family,” released on 19 July 1994. The “Smells Like Children” EP followed in 1995, featuring a cover of the Eurythmics’ “Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)”; Jeordie White, performing as Twiggy Ramirez, had by then replaced Gein on bass. “Antichrist Superstar” followed on 8 October 1996, co-produced by Reznor, Marilyn Manson, Dave Ogilvie and Sean Beavan, and debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 behind lead single “The Beautiful People.” The album’s success coincided with the departure of founding guitarist Daisy Berkowitz and the arrival of Zim Zum, and the band supported the record with the Dead to the World Tour. The group’s next album, “Mechanical Animals,” arrived on 15 September 1998, followed by “Holy Wood (In the Shadow of the Valley of Death)” in 2000, closing out the self-described triptych that “Antichrist Superstar” opened. Thirty years after its release, the album remains the first chapter of that trilogy.

items.body: This third album from the mysterious Swiss duo Blackbook was released just before the summer and brings us a total of 12 new tracks. I have always been somewhat intrigued by this act. While their music sounds superb, it is invariably driven by massive clichés and often seems almost literally ‘lifted’ from existing songs. With “Different”, they remain true to their 80s Electro-Wave/Pop influences, yet the tracks sound somewhat more personal this time around. It may be a cliché, but the way they develop their sound—consistently delivering strong choruses—is remarkable. Every single track sounds danceable and powerful, possessing the essential catchiness this genre demands. The songs also appear to have been deliberately kept short—not a single one reaches the four-minute mark. Blackbook remains a true mystery, yet one that consistently returns with great music—clichéd or not! (Rating:8½). Listen to “Nobody Loves You”: Nobody Loves You by Blackbook About Blackbook Blackbook is a Swiss duo who perform under masks and withhold their surnames, going only by their first names, Matthias and Albert. Both had previously played in other Swiss and German acts before forming Blackbook, citing 80s and 90s music as a shared influence. The duo discussed their approach and anonymity in a Side-Line interview in 2023. The project released a series of singles before compiling them into its official debut album, “Confessions Of The Innocent” (2023), followed by “Radio Strange” (2024) and, issued just before the summer of 2026, the duo’s third album “Different”, all released through darkTunes Music Group.

items.body: Side-Line Magazine has opened submissions for “Electronic Bodies 2,” the second volume in its electronic body music compilation series. Bands and artists making EBM and related electro-industrial styles can send in one track for consideration. The compilation will be released as a digital download via Side-Line’s Bandcamp page and promoted through Side-Line and its network of music media and DJs. The call follows “Electronic Bodies – Session 1”, Side-Line’s first EBM compilation, which brought together established names and lesser-known acts, covering old-school EBM, electro-industrial and more contemporary EBM styles. Electronic Bodies – Session 1 by Various Artists What Side-Line is looking for in ‘Electronic Bodies 2’ For this second installment, Side-Line is again looking for bands and artists making EBM, old-school industrial, electro-industrial and related electronic body music. Tracks built around pounding sequencers, aggressive basslines, mechanical rhythms or stripped-down electronic arrangements all fit the brief. New, unsigned and established acts are all welcome; selection is based on the music itself, not the size of an artist’s audience or the number of releases already out. How to submit a track for ‘Electronic Bodies 2’ Side-Line has set a few rules for submitting material, to be followed closely: Send one mastered track in WAV format, selecting the strongest material available. Submit it via WeTransfer.com to info@side-line.com; audio files sent as direct email attachments will not be accepted. Name the file using the format “Artist – Track Title.wav”. Artists must not be affiliated with GEMA, SABAM or similar collecting societies, since their licensing requirements could interfere with the compilation’s release. Artists selected for the compilation will be contacted to complete the necessary paperwork. Sending a track does not automatically guarantee inclusion; Side-Line will make a selection based on musical direction and the overall balance of the compilation. Submission deadline: November 30, 2026. The artwork accompanying this announcement is provisional and does not represent the final cover of “Electronic Bodies 2.” Side-Line will reveal the official artwork at a later stage. About the Electronic Bodies series Side-Line launched the Electronic Bodies series in January 2023, calling for submissions toward an old-school EBM compilation after a reader poll pointed the project at the early-1980s EBM sound of Belgium and its Scandinavian, Spanish and German counterparts, alongside New Beat tracks that fit the same mold. The project reached release on 1 September 2023 as “Electronic Bodies – Session 1,” an 88-track EBM charity compilation spanning EBM, New Beat and more contemporary offshoots, with all donations going to psychological support for Ukrainian soldiers and citizens affected by PTSD. Bernard Van Isacker, Side-Line’s chief editor, compiled the release and discussed the project in more detail with Side-Line ahead of its release. “Electronic Bodies 2” is the second volume in that series, with submissions open now.

items.body: Cleopatra Records will issue “Drink the New Wine”, the last studio recording by post-punk and goth rock band Bauhaus, as a 12-inch vinyl single on 30 October 2026. The pressing comes in three hand-numbered, etched color variants – white, silver and red – capped at 150 copies each, for a total of 450. Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins recorded the track separately during COVID-19 lockdown. The four traded audio files using the surrealist “exquisite corpse” method the band had used before. Bauhaus released it digitally in March 2022, its first new song since the 2008 album “Go Away White.” No Bauhaus recording has followed. Ash confirmed in April 2023 that the band’s reunion had ended, with the surviving members reforming Love and Rockets. ‘Drink the New Wine’: a lockdown recording now on hand-numbered vinyl Ash describes the track as typical of the band’s more playful side. “I always loved it when Bauhaus would go into art fart mode. Truly liberating and FUN!” he said. Cleopatra Records calls the release “a music artifact […] created for the most dedicated Bauhaus fans and collectors.” Side A of the single holds “Drink the New Wine.” Side B is etched with a reproduction of the Bauhaus logo and carries no audio. Each copy is individually hand-numbered, one color per customer, with no repressing planned once the 450 copies sell out. The single is available for pre-order through Cleopatra Records ahead of the 30 October release. About Bauhaus Small Wonder Records released Bauhaus’s debut single, “Bela Lugosi’s Dead,” in August 1979, a year after Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash, David J (David John Haskins) and his younger brother Kevin Haskins formed the band in Northampton, England. The single arrived before goth existed as a named scene. Four studio albums followed in four years on 4AD and Beggars Banquet: “In the Flat Field” (1980), “Mask” (1981), “The Sky’s Gone Out” (1982) and “Burning from the Inside” (1983). Bauhaus split on 5 July 1983, a week before “Burning from the Inside” reached shops. The pioneering band reunited for a 1998 tour and again from 2005 to 2008, a run that produced a fifth album, “Go Away White” (2008, Cooking Vinyl), released without a supporting tour. Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins had already carried their partnership into Love and Rockets, formed in 1985, and into separate solo careers. David J’s catalog includes the albums “Etiquette of Violence” and “Songs from Another Season,” plus a 2014 memoir, “Who Killed Mister Moonlight?” The four original members reunited again in 2019, announcing Peter Murphy’s first live date with Bauhaus after a heart attack ahead of shows at the Hollywood Palladium that November. A further reunion tour followed in 2022, covering Europe and the US West Coast. Months after the band released “Drink the New Wine,” Murphy’s rehab admission forced it to cancel the rest of its North American tour that August. Ash ended the reunion in April 2023, and the surviving trio returned to Love and Rockets. David J has stayed active since. He revisited his own archive on the album ‘Tracks From the Attic Revisited’ and discussed the project earlier this year in a Side-Line interview. This is the first time “Drink the New Wine” has been pressed to a physical format.

items.body: Front Line Assembly’s “Epitaph” turns 25 this year. Metropolis Records released the electro-industrial and EBM album on 8 October 2001, the eleventh full-length studio album by the Vancouver band led by Bill Leeb and Chris Peterson. The record marked Front Line Assembly‘s return to Metropolis Records after the band left the label in October 1999. “Epitaph” runs ten tracks and 54:57, recorded at Cryogenic Studio and produced by Leeb and Peterson. Greg Reely handled mixing and engineering, Brian Gardner mastered the album, and Dave McKean supplied the artwork and design. The tracklist runs “Haloed”, “Dead Planet”, “Backlash”, “Epitaph”, “Everything Must Perish”, “Conscience”, “Decoy”, “Insolence”, “Krank It Up” and “Existance”, the last of which folds in the hidden track “Submerged” after a minute of silence. Metropolis also issued a digipak edition limited to 25,000 copies carrying that bonus track. “Everything Must Perish”, released 11 September 2001, was the only single taken from the album. Bill Leeb told Side-Line at the time that “Epitaph” broke with the band’s earlier reliance on film dialogue samples: “This is the first time we quit using movie samples.” He added: “Sampling is an artform which was criticised in the beginning, but now it’s a respected artform with big money in it. It’s a big business where I don’t feel at ease any longer.” Artoffact Records re-released ‘Epitaph’ on limited edition vinyl in 2015. About Front Line Assembly Bill Leeb founded Front Line Assembly in Vancouver, British Columbia, in 1986 after leaving Skinny Puppy, where he had performed under the stage name Wilhelm Schroeder. Rhys Fulber worked with Leeb from the same period as an early, unofficial collaborator, and Michael Balch became an official member on keyboards and programming in 1988. The band’s debut album, “The Initial Command”, came out on the Belgian label KK at the end of 1987, followed by “State of Mind” on the German label Dossier in January 1988 and “Corrosion” the same year, licensed to Wax Trax! for North America. Balch left after the Gashed Senses & Crossfire tour in 1989 to join Ministry and Revolting Cocks, and Fulber stepped in as an official member. “Gashed Senses & Crossfire” (1989) gave the band its first chart entry, with “Digital Tension Dementia” reaching No. 45 on Billboard’s Hot Dance Club Songs. “Caustic Grip” followed in 1990, the album that began Front Line Assembly’s long-running partnership with mixer and engineer Greg Reely and introduced more guitar-driven material. Chris Peterson debuted as a live percussionist on the accompanying tour before later becoming a full-time member. “Tactical Neural Implant” (1992) brought a more melodic, sample-heavy direction, and “Millennium” (1994) became the band’s first industrial metal record, featuring session guitar from Devin Townsend, who also played on “Hard Wired” (1995). Fulber left in 1997 to concentrate on producing Fear Factory, and Peterson took over his role as the band moved toward the electronica and big-beat leanings of “[FLA]vour of the Weak” (1997) and “Implode” (1999). In October 1999 the band left Metropolis Records; “Epitaph”, produced by Leeb and Peterson and issued on 8 October 2001, marked its return to that label. Peterson departed after finishing work on the album, and Fulber rejoined in 2003 for “Civilization” (2004). Beyond the main discography, Leeb has led the side project Delerium since 1987, and members have worked on Noise Unit, Conjure One (Fulber), Cyberaktif (Leeb with Skinny Puppy’s cEvin Key and Dwayne Goettel) and other spin-offs. Front Line Assembly went on to release “Artificial Soldier” (2006), “Improvised Electronic Device” (2010), “Echogenetic” (2013), “Wake Up the Coma” (2019) and “Mechanical Soul” (2021), the last featuring guest appearances from Jean-Luc De Meyer of Front 242 and Dino Cazares of Fear Factory. The band caught up with Side-Line on the state of the group in 2024, with Leeb and Fulber both still in the current lineup. “Epitaph” remains the band’s eleventh studio album and, twenty-five years on, the record that reopened its relationship with Metropolis Records.

items.body: 『声なき声のドローイング:スキャン画像』2026［© Shu Yonezawa, Courtesy of SNOW Contemporary］ 会期：2026/07/17～2026/09/05 会場：SNOW Contemporary［東京都］ 公式サイト：http://snowcontemporary.com/exhibition/202607.html （前編から） ステートメントには続けて「彩度は低く細かな色相の差異で描いたのはキャラクターと捉えるには薄く複雑な声未満の存在であ」ったと書かれている。米澤は以前から、キャラクターの「声」に関心を寄せてきた。実際、キャラクターのアイデンティティを規定するうえで声はイメージと同等以上に重要な役割を果たしているだろう。しかし米澤が声に見出しているのは、もっと広い可能性であるようにも思われる──アニマとキャラクターのあいだを自由に往還する現象としての可能性を。 そもそも“anima”が「魂」と同時に「息」や「風」を意味する語であったことを思い出そう。 神が息を吹き込むこと （ インスピレーション ） によって事物はアニメートされる。世界を巡る空気の流れが振動としてあらわれたものが声だと考えるなら、それはまさにアニマをもっとも色濃く反映した現象だと言えるだろう。無論、この魂-呼吸-声といった直線的な繋がりは、あくまでも西欧的な生命観にもとづくものであることに注意しなければならない。例えばアーティストの布施琳太郎は、米澤が描く「オバケ」状のキャラクターにおいてしばしば口が身体（構造）から遊離していることを指摘し、ここにアニマと声のより自由な関係の可能性を見ている★3。すなわち、ヤツメウナギなどに代表される無顎類が摂食のための口と呼吸のための鰓を完全に独立して発達させたように、米澤のキャラクター表現は、私たちが生物学的な人体構造によって規定されているがゆえに硬直してしまったアニマとの関係性を、いまひとたびときほぐすことを試みているのではないか、と★4。 自由に泳ぎ回る口があらゆる場所で開き、声を発する。もはやこのとき、「口」を画面内に描かれた身体パーツのみに限定する理由はない。むしろ米澤作品はつねに「口」そのものとともに存在してきたとも言えるだろう——フレームという口として。キャンバス、トレーシングペーパー、ビニール、モニタ、スクリーン——手法や素材の別によらず、米澤の作品は基本的に矩形の画面を前提としているように見える。特に本展では、これまでビニール自体をピンで固定する形式を主としてきた「アニマの通り跡」シリーズがアルミフレームに張られ、壁や空中に吊られている。また、映像を主とするインスタレーション的な作品《別の海としての身体》では、小型のモニタが半透明のアクリルケースによってさらにフレーミングされ、スピーカー——もっとも象徴的な機械の口——だけが隣接する壁面にさまよい出ている。とはいえ、アニメーション表現を背景に持つ米澤が矩形のフレームを意識するのは当然のことであり、そうした強固な枠があればこそ、不定形に蠢くアニマたちの流出もまた強調されるのだ、と言うことはできるだろう。ではその上で、あらゆる場所に開かれるフレームを「口」とみなすことはどんな意味を持つのか。 ［撮影：木奥惠三］ そもそも人間の発生に限ってみても、口とは「顔に開いた穴」などではない。妊娠初期にあたる8週から12週ごろ、胎児の顔部では、周囲から伸び上がってきた突起が中央で癒合することによって口唇や口蓋がつくられ、口の輪郭が完成する。口とはほんらい、開くものではなく、意図的に閉じ損なったものなのだ。最初はすべてが穴であり、その穴が埋められていく過程で残された残余としてのみ、口は定義しうる。ここで、白川静が「口」という漢字の成り立ちについて唱えた次のような説が思い出される。いわく、口は人間の開いた口唇ではなく、祝詞をおさめる器（サイ）のかたちに由来するのだと。学問的な信憑性に疑問はあるものの、解釈としては興味深い。すなわち、口を漢字練習帳のマス目のような「文字の到来を待つ空白」そのものの象形として捉えるなら、それは「いまだ閉じられていないこと」それ自体を意味する。そしてその「閉じられていない」という事実こそが、声を召喚する。口が声を発するのではない。むしろあらかじめ世界に満ちているそれが、たまたま口が見出されたときに受信され、声としてあらわれるのだ。この意味において、世界のあちこちに口を見出すことはそのまま声を見出すことであり、米澤が言うところの「アニメーション」概念のもっとも素朴なかたちであるように思える★5。 最後に、広義の「口」の観点から、米澤の代表的なモチーフである目についても考えておこう。目の本質を眼球ではなく、それが収まる眼窩やまぶたといった立体的なフレームに置いてみると、そこにはひとつの水槽のようなものが浮かび上がってくる。眼球というアニマが泳ぐ、涙で満たされた水槽が。口が開閉するように、目はまばたきを行なう。まばたきは視界を寸断して不完全な視覚をつくり出すが、同時に眼球を涙液でコーティングし、目を開き続けることで生じる像のブレを修正してもいる。つまり、視覚をいくつものフレームに分割する行為によってこそ、眼球はかろうじて息をしている。まばたきとは、目に許されたただひとつの呼吸であり、同時にこの器官が「閉じ損ねている」ことの証でもある。では果たして、完全な視界＝ずっと目を開き続ける視界などというものはありえるのだろうか。もしありえるのならばそのとき、一体なにが見えるのだろうか。 ［撮影：木奥惠三］ ここまでの議論をふまえると、本展は展示室に開いた口から流れ込んだアニマたちが、室内のあちらこちらに思い思いの像をあらわしていくひとつの現象として捉えられる——その構造はさながら、写真機の原型としての「 暗い部屋 （ カメラ・オブスキュラ ） 」を思わせる。しかし冒頭で述べたとおり、本展はむしろ光で満たされた「明るい部屋」としてあらわれている。ただしそれは、事物の輪郭を切り分ける乾いた光ではなく、目を凝らすほどにそのイメージを滲ませる湿った光、水底で感じる明るさに近い。波間でゆらぎ、水を透過して散乱した光が絶えず私たちの目を幻惑する。言葉遊びを許すなら「 水妖の部屋 （ カメラ・オブ・スキュラ ） 」とでも言えようか。水妖&efDotアニマは気ままに水と光の中に溶けてまわり、そのゆらめきのあいだに身を翻す。あちこちで口が開いては何ごとかをつぶやき、また消え去っていく。私の口もそれにつられて開くのだが、ごぼごぼと水音を立てるばかりで上手く喋れない。いや、そこでは私の口を借りて水妖たちの声があらわれているのだ。私がまだその声を捉えることができないというだけで。ぱくぱくと単調に開閉を繰り返すだけの口の動きは、再生か逆再生かを区別できない。それゆえに、時間は渦を巻いてほどけていく。水に包まれた私の目はまばたきを忘れ、ただ見開かれている。 ★3──布施琳太郎「無顎類のアニマ：キャラクターアートの終焉の後で」（米澤柊『泳ぐ目たちのアーカイヴ』所収、2026） ★4──私たち人間を思わせる身体パーツや骨格構造をところどころに有しつつも、中心性は不確かで、不定形に広がっている──こうした米澤作品におけるキャラクターの比喩として、私がまっさきに思いついたのはホヤであった。ホヤは尾索動物に属し、私たち脊椎動物と比較的近縁の生物である。オタマジャクシ型の幼生時は脳や脊索を備え、遊泳しながら住処を探す。この時点では摂食を行なわないため口はなく（眼点や嗅覚細胞の原型は存在するものの）器官としての目や鼻もない。そして無事、岩などを見つけるとそこに固着し、よく知られたホヤの形になる。脳や脊索、眼点を失う代わりに大きな口が開き、水を漉し取って栄養を摂取するだけの存在となる。いわばホヤは、脊椎動物的な身体構造を幼生から成体までのタイムスケールのなかに散在させている生物として捉えられる。言い換えれば、ホヤを時間的に再構成したものとして人間を考えることもできるだろう。 ★5──ここまで見てきた要素をまとめると、米澤の作品は、暗黙化した身体感覚／構造を再構成することを通じて、私たちが不可知化してしまったアニマを汲み上げようとしているのだといえる。そこには目（視覚）や声（聴覚）に加え、手指のモチーフを通じた触覚的なイメージや、米澤が「イメージの骨／アニメーションの骨」といった言い回しで示唆する、抽象的な身体感覚なども含まれている。しかし、嗅覚的な要素に限ってはあまり読み取れない。そもそも、米澤の描くキャラクター表象において鼻の存在感はきわめて希薄だ。横顔においてわずかに隆起らしきものが確認できるが、正面顔では鼻、とりわけ鼻孔はほぼ捨象されている。鼻は脊椎動物に特有の器官であり、もともと大脳は嗅覚情報処理のために大きく発達したのだとも言われている。 鑑賞日：2026/07/25（土）
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于米澤柊个展「声なき声のキャラクター」的艺术评论，而非音乐评论。文章围绕展览中的动画、绘画与影像作品展开哲学性论述，核心议题是「口」与「声」的关系：从字符学角度重新解读「口」的象形意义，到生物学层面探讨呼吸与摄食器官的分化，再到将画面矩形边框本身视为「口」的隐喻。作者援引布施琳太郎对无颌类的论述、白川静的汉字学说等，将展览空间比作「水妖的房间」，强调声音与气息作为生命表征的流动性。整体为视觉艺术与哲学批评的交叉写作，与音乐关联薄弱，风格标签偏向前卫艺术与装置/动画领域。
